questions.q_text: Because Mr. Chang has been busy these days, it's _______ whether he will come to the party.

options.D: inevitable

explanation.translation: 因為張先生最近很忙，所以他是否會來參加派對還很令人懷疑。
explanation.analysis:
空格後接 whether (是否)，表示不確定的事情。it is doubtful whether... 為常見句型。
(A) unlikely 通常接 to V。
(D) inevitable 語意不符。

questions.q_text: I'm quite _______ to the weather in Taiwan, so I think I'll stay here for another year.

options.D: accustomed

explanation.translation: 我相當習慣台灣的天氣，所以我想我會在這裡多待一年。
explanation.analysis:
(D) be accustomed to + N/Ving，表示「習慣於...」。
(A) devoted to (致力於)，不能說奉獻給天氣。

questions.q_text: Mr. Smith won't tolerate talking during class; he says it _______ others.

explanation.translation: Smith 先生不容許上課講話；他說這會打擾到其他人。
explanation.analysis:
(A) disturb (打擾)，符合語境。
(B) deserve (應得)。
(D) dismiss (解散)。

questions.q_text: On the basis of the clues, can you predict the _______ of the story?

options.A: outcome

explanation.translation: 根據這些線索，你能預測故事的結局嗎？
explanation.analysis:
(A) outcome (結局/結果)，符合語意。
(B) headline (新聞標題)。

questions.q_text: A good reader can often figure out what new words mean by using _______.

options.B: context

explanation.translation: 一個好的閱讀者通常能透過使用上下文來推斷新單字的意思。
explanation.analysis:
(B) context (上下文)，這是閱讀測驗的核心技巧。
(A) contact (接觸)。
(C) content (內容)。

questions.q_text: I wonder why she _______ turned up the radio when I was studying.

options.A: sympathetically
options.C: deliberately
options.D: thoroughly

explanation.translation: 我想知道為什麼當我在讀書時，她要故意把收音機開大聲。
explanation.analysis:
(C) deliberately (故意地) 符合影響他人讀書的語境。
(A) sympathetically (同情地)。
(D) thoroughly (徹底地)。

questions.q_text: It suddenly _______ me that I had to get to the airport to meet a friend.

options.B: struck

explanation.translation: 我突然想起我必須去機場接朋友。
explanation.analysis: 固定句型 It strikes someone that... 表示「某人突然想起...」。若要選 (C)，需搭配介系詞 to，即 It occurred to me that...。

questions.q_text: Being a very careful person, he is quite _______ in giving his comments.

options.A: reserved
options.B: melancholy

explanation.translation: 身為一個非常謹慎的人，他在給予評論時相當保留/拘謹。
explanation.analysis:
(A) reserved (保留的/謹言慎行的)，呼應前文的 careful person。
(B) melancholy (憂鬱的)。

questions.q_text: Most viewers agreed that the movie _______ was not as good as the book.

options.B: version

explanation.translation: 大多數觀眾同意這部電影版本不如原著小說好看。
explanation.analysis:
(B) movie version (電影版本)。
(A) routine (例行公事)。
(D) issue (議題/期號)。

questions.q_text: The native greeted the travelers in a _______ language which was strange to them.

options.C: peculiar

explanation.translation: 當地人用一種對旅客來說很陌生的奇怪語言向他們打招呼。
explanation.analysis:
(C) peculiar (奇怪的/特有的)，呼應後文的 strange。
(A) contrary (相反的)。
(D) spiral (螺旋的)。

groups.passage_translation:
雨傘並不是一項新發明。中國人在西元前十一世紀就已經有了雨傘。從中國，雨傘傳到了印度、波斯和埃及。但是在希臘和羅馬，男人是不會使用雨傘的。他們認為雨傘只是給女人用的。

當西班牙探險家前往墨西哥時，他們看到阿茲特克的國王正在使用雨傘。英國探險家也發現在北美洲東岸的印第安王子也會攜帶雨傘。似乎世界各地的人們在不同的時間都發明了雨傘。

英國可能是歐洲第一個由普通百姓撐傘來擋雨的國家。英國的氣候多雨，所以雨傘在那裡非常實用。

雨傘現在是一件非常普遍的物品。今天每個人都在使用它。它可以為人們擋雨遮陽。有些雨傘可以折疊，所以很容易攜帶。

explanation.translation: 中國人在西元前十一世紀就有了雨傘。

explanation.translation: 從中國，它們傳播到了印度...

explanation.translation: 男人不會使用它們。
explanation.analysis: 全文為過去式，配合語意選 wouldn't。

explanation.translation: 他們認為雨傘只是給女人用的。

explanation.analysis: 感官動詞 saw + 受詞 + Ving。

explanation.translation: 似乎世界各地的人...
explanation.analysis: It seems that + 子句 為固定句型。

explanation.translation: 英國可能是歐洲第一個普通人撐傘的國家（在那裡普通人撐傘）。
explanation.analysis: 先行詞為 country，需用關係副詞 where。

explanation.translation: 用雨傘來抵擋雨水。
explanation.analysis: 介系詞 against 有「防禦、抵抗」之意。

explanation.translation: 雨傘現在是非常普通的物品。

explanation.translation: 有些雨傘可以折疊，所以很容易攜帶。
explanation.analysis: 前句為因，後句為果，選 so。

groups.passage:
Most heroes are people like you. But what makes them heroes? They find special courage when they need it. They are brave enough to help in an emergency while others may stand by. A hero sees what needs to be done and does it.

Sometimes heroes are rewarded for their brave acts. One such reward is the Carnegie Medal. It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.

The medal was named after Andrew Carnegie. In 1886, Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter who lost his life trying to save two other boys from drowning. Carnegie became a very rich businessman and set aside money to honor heroes like William.
groups.passage_translation:
大多數的英雄都是像你我一樣的普通人。但到底是什麼讓他們成為英雄呢？他們在需要的時候會找到特別的勇氣。在緊急情況下，當其他人可能只會袖手旁觀時，他們卻夠勇敢去幫忙。英雄看見需要被完成的事情，並且付諸實行。

有時候，英雄們會因為他們的勇敢行為而獲得獎勵。其中一項獎勵就是卡內基獎章。它是頒發給那些勇敢行動，並面對危險以拯救他人生命的人。

這枚獎章是以安德魯·卡內基的名字命名的。在1886年，卡內基聽說了一位名叫威廉·亨特的年輕人，他為了救另外兩個快溺水的男孩而失去了自己的生命。卡內基後來成為了一位非常富有的商人，並撥出一筆錢來表揚像威廉這樣的英雄。

questions.q_text: The Carnegie Medal is given to those who are _______

explanation.translation: 卡內基獎章頒給那些無私且有勇氣的人。
explanation.analysis: (D) 根據第二段，獎章頒給「冒險拯救他人生命的人」，即無私(unselfish)與勇敢(courageous)。

questions.q_text: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: William Hunter was a very brave boy.
options.C: Some heroes have been rewarded for their bravery.
options.D: Carnegie was a rich businessman and liked to help people.

explanation.translation: 這篇文章的主旨是什麼？
explanation.analysis: (C) 貫穿全文，首段講英雄特質，後段介紹卡內基獎章如何「獎勵英雄的勇敢」。

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.B: Brave deeds can take many different forms.
options.C: Over 6,000 people are Carnegie Medal recipients.
options.D: Some heroes have received money as well as the Medal.

explanation.translation: 下列哪項敘述是錯誤的？
explanation.analysis: (A) 文章第三段說 Carnegie 'heard about' (聽說過) William Hunter，代表他們並不認識 (not in person)。此為錯誤敘述，故選A。

groups.passage:
On May 26, 1977, George Willig traveled to the top of the 1,350-foot-tall World Trade Center in New York City. He did not take the elevator, however. Instead, like a human fly, George Willig climbed the outside of the immense 110-story building. His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.

At the top, Willig was greeted by both police and reporters. Some of the police officers asked him for his autograph. Then they wanted to put him in jail and charged him with violation of law for climbing the building without a permit...
groups.passage_translation:
1977年5月26日，喬治·威利格到了紐約市1350英尺高的世貿中心頂樓。然而，他沒有搭乘電梯。相反地，他就像一隻「人蠅」一樣，徒手攀爬了這棟高達110層樓的巨大建築的外部。他的攀登行動從早上6點30分開始，花了三個半小時才完成。

到達頂樓時，迎接威利格的是警察和記者。有些警察甚至向他要了簽名。但隨後他們就想把他關進監獄，並以無照攀爬建築物而指控他違法...

questions.q_text: George Willig reached the top of the World Trade Center in New York at

options.A: six thirty in the morning of May 26, 1977.
options.B: six thirty in the evening of May 26, 1977.
options.C: ten o'clock in the morning of May 26, 1977.
options.D: ten o'clock in the evening of May 26, 1977.

explanation.translation: 喬治·威利格到達世貿中心頂樓的時間是？
explanation.analysis: (C) 早上 6:30 開始爬，花了三個半小時，所以是 早上 10 點到達。

questions.q_text: This passage is a story about

options.A: a man who enjoys dangers and risks.
options.B: a human being who can fly like a fly.
options.C: a man who has escaped from the jail.
options.D: a fly which climbs like a human being.

explanation.translation: 這篇文章是關於？
explanation.analysis: (A) 關於一個享受危險與冒險的男人。

questions.q_text: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.B: Willig was sent to prison for a year.
options.C: Willig was honored in a party and fined only $1.10.
options.D: Willig climbed the World Trade Center with permission.

explanation.translation: 根據文章，下列哪項敘述為真？
explanation.analysis: (C) 文章最後指出，市長不但沒有懲罰他，反而每層樓只象徵性罰他一便士 (共 $1.10)，並表揚他。

groups.passage:
Printing is one of the most important means of communication. Without it you would not now be reading this passage. Even the development of radio and television has not diminished the importance of printing.

The first printing was done from wood blocks one letter at a time by hand. This was a slow process, requiring much skill and patience... A great step forward was the use of movable type. The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century...

One of the first European books to be printed in movable type was Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible. The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy. It was printed in Flanders in 1474 by an Englishman, William Caxton...
groups.passage_translation:
印刷術是最重要的通訊方式之一。沒有它，你現在就不會讀到這篇文章。即使是廣播和電視的發展，也沒有削弱印刷術的重要性。

最早的印刷是用木塊手工一次刻一個字母。這是一個緩慢的過程，需要大量的技巧和耐心... 向前邁出的一大步是活字印刷的使用。中國人在11世紀發現了這個技術...

歐洲第一批用活字印刷的書籍之一是約翰尼斯·谷登堡的四十二行聖經。第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書是關於特洛伊的歷史。它是由英國人威廉·卡克斯頓於1474年在法蘭德斯印刷的...

questions.q_text: Printing is important because

options.B: it has made reading books possible.
options.C: it has helped to develop radio and television.
options.D: William Caxton printed 80 books in English.

explanation.translation: 印刷術很重要因為？
explanation.analysis: (B) 根據第一段，沒有印刷術就無法閱讀文章，意即它讓閱讀書籍成為可能。

questions.q_text: The use of movable type was first introduced by

explanation.translation: 活字印刷術最早是由誰引進的？
explanation.analysis: (D) 第二段指出 The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century。

questions.q_text: According to the passage, the use of movable type was considered as a "great step forward" because

options.A: it did not need a lot of wood.
options.B: it required less skill and patience.
options.C: the printing letters could be reused.
options.D: every page of every book required individual carving.

explanation.translation: 為何活字印刷被視為「一大進步」？
explanation.analysis: (C) 因為舊方法每頁都要獨立雕刻，而活字印刷可以重新排列字母來印別的東西 (reused)。

questions.q_text: The first English book printed in movable type was

options.A: done from wood blocks one letter at a time.
options.B: done in a printing press at Westminster.

explanation.translation: 第一本用活字印刷的英文書是？
explanation.analysis: (D) 第三段提到 The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy。
